reminder.title: Reporting aircraft defects
reminder.intro: All pilots and users are reminded of the importance of immediately reporting any defect, damage, or anomaly detected on an aircraft.
checklist: Any issue, even minor, must be reported to operations and maintenance.
This includes cracks, missing fasteners, and any other abnormal condition detected.
Early reporting allows the issue to be assessed and resolved before the next flight.
reminder.callout: Do not assume the defect has already been reported by someone else.
howToReport: Speak directly to maintenance or hangar staff
Submit a squawk through Flight Radar
Where appropriate, submit a safety report via QR code

procedure.title: Safety Bulletin: In-flight alternator failure
procedure.summary: Reminder of the basic procedure for an in-flight alternator failure. Quick, orderly action is essential to conserve battery, keep essential equipment running, and return safely.

steps.title: Cycle alternator
steps.detail: Alternator and master: OFF then ON. Check whether charge indication (amps/volts) returns to normal.

steps.title: Check circuit breakers
steps.detail: If breakers are in and the warning light stays on, alternator failure is confirmed.

steps.title: Reduce electrical load
steps.detail: Turn off unnecessary lights. Transponder off if needed to conserve battery.

steps.title: Communicate
steps.detail: Inform ATC, declare PAN PAN, state alternator failure, advise return to field.

steps.title: Decide
steps.detail: Return to departure airport or divert to the nearest suitable field.

procedure.photoAlt: Instrument panel with the alternator warning light illuminated
procedure.warning: An inoperative alternator can cause loss of essential equipment. Act quickly and follow the procedure.

reference.title: Applicable minimum altitudes
reference.intro: Reminder of the legal and internal minimum altitudes applicable to VFR flights and school operations.

rows.situation: Day VFR over cities, towns, or gatherings
rows.minimum: 1,000 ft above the highest obstacle within 600 m

rows.situation: Day VFR in all other areas
rows.minimum: 500 ft above ground/water, or 500 ft above obstacles within 150 m
2,000 ft above the highest obstacle within 8 km

rows.situation: Night VFR in all other areas
rows.minimum: 1,000 ft above the highest obstacle within 8 km
1,000 ft above any obstacle within 5 NM
2,000 ft above any obstacle within 8 NM

maintenance.textA: On these aircraft the oil cap and dipstick are separate parts. After the check, make sure both are correctly installed.
maintenance.textB: During the check, leave the oil cap in a visible place on the outer surface so it prevents the cowling from closing — a reminder to reinstall it.
